stemMd: How could the square be welcoming and difficult to cross without either account being dishonest?

options.label: A
options.textMd: All memories must describe exactly the same instant.

options.label: B
options.textMd: One account must be invented whenever two views differ.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Different people could encounter different aspects or conditions of the same place.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Traffic and social activity cannot coexist.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Photographs always prove every memory false.

explanationMd: A place can enable social meetings while posing mobility difficulties, and conditions can change over time. The accounts need not be mutually exclusive once their contexts are understood. Difference alone does not establish deception.

distractorRationale.a: The colleague suggests different periods and times.
distractorRationale.b: The passage offers contextual explanations instead.
distractorRationale.e: Photographs are presented alongside memories, not as automatic refutations.
distractorRationale.d: A space can have both characteristics.
